pages.text: Picked olives filled a big tray. They would choose the plump ones to soak in salt water.
Lulu pulled up an empty basket and sat down. "I will choose the plump ones."
Uncle Beppo brought a round, hole-filled sieve. "In our day, we sorted them quickly with this."
He shook it gently. Rattle, rattle.
Oh! Big olives and small olives all fell onto the tray. The holes were too large.
"Has the sieve grown old...?" He held it to his eyes and peered through. His eyes blinked through the holes.
All the olives were mixed again. He set the sieve down.
Lulu picked up one at a time. Plump ones in the basket, small ones in a bowl.
Shiny, plump olives filled Lulu's basket.
Uncle Beppo quietly sat beside Lulu and began picking them up one by one. Soon there were two baskets of plump olives.
